name: Eurycomanone
description: Eurycomanone (CAS 84633-29-4 ), also known as pasakbumin A, is a quassinoid compound isolated from Eurycoma longifolia root extract. It is the primary bioactive marker used to standardize botanical extracts for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications. Consistent potency and traceability are critical procurement considerations for this compound. In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, it serves as the quantitative reference standard against which root extracts are graded and quality-controlled. Pharmaceutical and biotechnology researchers source it as an analytical reference compound for HPLC method development, assay validation, and bioactivity screening programs. This ensures high precision in laboratory testing environments. Standardized botanical extract suppliers use this content, typically expressed as a percentage, as the primary specification differentiator between extract grades. This allows for clear benchmarking during the procurement process. In life sciences research, it is procured for in vitro studies investigating cellular and enzymatic mechanisms. These studies support early-stage drug discovery pipelines and help validate therapeutic claims for finished products. The compound is supplied as a purified solid, typically as a white to off-white powder at high purity levels of 95 to 99 percent. This level of purity is suited for reference standard and research applications requiring USP or EP alignment. It is available in research quantities through specialty fine chemical and botanical extract suppliers.
